newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Malta to explain EU stance in Brussels.
newsitem.headline: Malta to explain EU stance in Brussels.

text.p: Malta will explain to the European Union on Monday what its plans are for EU membership following the election last month of a government pledged to drop the bid.

The Labour government of Prime Minister Alfred Sant, sworn in on October 29, ran on a platform of withdrawing the tiny Mediterranean island's application for EU membership and its links with NATO through the Partnership for Peace programme.
EU diplomats said Malta had not yet withdrawn its application although it had effectively frozen its bid by saying it would no longer take part in regular taolks between the two sides.
The first such talks since the election were due to take place in Brussels on Tuesday.
Instead, Deputy Prime Minister George Vella is to meet EU foreign ministers on the margins of a scheduled EU meeting on Monday to discuss future ties.
EU officials said they had detected something of a softening in the Maltese stance since the new government took office.
They said they believed Malta may want to keep its options open, putting the application on hold rather than withdrawing it altogether.
Malta is one of 12 countries in eastern Europe and the Mediterranean to be told they can become EU members at a later date. Formal talks are due to begin towards the beginning of 1998.
